title: Block Vendor Edits
summary: A Claude Code hook that denies edits to files inside node_modules, vendor and dist folders, so fixes go to your own source and not copies.
description: Changes made inside an installed package or a build folder disappear on the next install or build. This PreToolUse hook checks the path of each Edit or Write and refuses it when a folder named node_modules, vendor or dist is part of it.
The error text points the agent back at your own sources. Windows and Unix paths are both handled.
useWhen: Stop agents from patching a dependency in place
Keep compiled output out of your diffs
Work in a repo with a checked-in vendor folder
Make bug fixes land in real source files

hook.command: node -e "process.on('uncaughtException',()=>process.exit(0));let d='';process.stdin.on('data',c=>d+=c).on('end',()=>{let j={};try{j=JSON.parse(d)||{}}catch(e){process.exit(0)}const i=j.tool_input||{};const f=String(i.file_path||'');const fs=require('fs');const p=f.split(String.fromCharCode(92)).join('/');const m=p.match(new RegExp('(^|/)(node_modules|vendor|dist)/'));if(m){console.error('Blocked: '+f+' is inside '+m[2]+'. Edit the source files or the package version instead, never the installed or built copy.');process.exit(2)}process.exit(0)})"

example.prompt: The date parsing bug is in node_modules/dayjs, fix it there.
example.result: The edit is refused. The agent proposes a version bump, a patch file or a wrapper in your own code.

faq.question: Does it block reading those folders?
faq.answer: No. It only watches Edit and Write, so the agent can still read dependency code to understand a bug.

faq.question: What about a build folder with another name?
faq.answer: Only node_modules, vendor and dist are matched. Add more names inside the pattern in the command for others.

access: Reads the file path of each edit
Blocks matching paths; changes no files
